Numbering Our Days

December 29, 2025

Numbering Our Days

 

Scripture: “So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom.” — Psalm 90:12

 

Thought: A new year has a way of creating illusions. We imagine we’ve been handed something clean, untouched, full of potential—as if time itself will save us. But Scripture is far less sentimental. Moses does not pray for more days; he prays for wisdom within them.

 

To number our days is not morbid; it is clarifying. It reminds us that time is not a renewable resource. Every day that passes is a day spent, not stored. The tragedy is not that life is short, but that it is often wasted—drifted through without intention or obedience.

 

The new year invites us to wake up. Not to panic, but to pay attention. A man who understands his mortality does not live recklessly; he lives deliberately. Wisdom begins when we stop assuming we have time.

 

Reflection: What did last year reveal about how you spend your days?

 

Call to Action: Write down three ways you want to spend your time this year. Be specific [these are not resolutions or just goals you want to achieve].

 

Prayer: “Lord, teach me to live awake. Help me treat my days as gifts, not guarantees. Give me a heart of wisdom. Amen.”
